sprain.title: Sprain
sprain.advice: Rest it and try not to put weight on it. Put a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours, and keep it raised on a pillow. If you can't put any weight on it, or it looks badly swollen or out of shape, please get it checked by a doctor.

cut.title: Small cut
cut.advice: Press on it with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding, then rinse it with clean water and cover it with a bandage. If it's deep, keeps bleeding after 10 minutes of pressure, or was made by something rusty, please see a doctor.

burn.title: Minor burn
burn.advice: Cool it under cool running water for about 20 minutes. Don't put ice, butter or toothpaste on it. Then cover it loosely with a clean cloth. If it's large, on your face, or blistering badly, please see a doctor.

bruise.title: Bump or bruise
bruise.advice: Put a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it for about 15 minutes, and rest it. It should feel better in a few days. If the pain is very bad or it doesn't improve, please see a doctor.

nosebleed.title: Nosebleed
nosebleed.advice: Sit up, lean slightly forward, and pinch the soft part of your nose for 10 to 15 minutes. Don't tilt your head back. If it doesn't stop after 20 minutes, please get medical help.

dizzy.title: Feeling dizzy
dizzy.advice: Please sit or lie down right away so you don't fall, and breathe slowly. Take a few small sips of water, and get up slowly once it passes. If it comes with chest pain, a very bad headache, fainting, or trouble speaking, call 112 right away.

nausea.title: Feeling sick
nausea.advice: Sit upright and rest, and take small sips of water often so you don't get dehydrated. Avoid heavy food for a while. If you can't keep any water down, see blood, or it lasts more than a day, please see a doctor.

cramps.title: Period cramps
cramps.advice: A warm water bottle or heating pad on your lower belly can help, along with rest, gentle stretching and sips of water. If the pain is severe, unusual for you, or stops you from doing everyday things, please see a doctor.
